Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who is your favorite stormtrooper from the star wars franchise (Finn is allowed)?
Answer: My favourite Stormtrooper is from the Expanded Universe, and was the original inspiration for the Darktroopers, as seen in The Mandalorian. Long before Moff Gideon and his Imperial Remnants unleashed the Darktrooper droids on baby Grogu, their was a General in the Imperial Army who firstly had the idea of cybernetically enhanced suits for his stormtroopers. Rom Mohc was a decorated war hero of the Clone Wars, then turned hero of the Empire after the fall of the Republic. He eventually overseen production of the revolutionary Dark Trooper Project. This top secret project was developed to create the ultimate evolution for the standard Stormtrooper. Below; Darth Vader himself gives his approval at General Mohcs work. The Empire had already designed a Darktrooper soldier, resulting in the Phase Zero Darktroopers, which were more a macabre zombie version of a Stormtrooper. It's purpose was to produce a soldier that had all the on field skills and initiative of a clone commando, coupled with the immense firepower of a B-Series Battle Droid. They eventually evolved into the Phase 1 and 2 versions of the Stormtrooper suit, but Phase 3 was something else entirely. Above;(from left to right) Darktrooper Phase I, Phase II, and Phase III. Using remnants left over from the technology that transformed Anakin Skywalker into a cybernetic monster the Empire concieved cybernetic warriors, who initially were clone veterans. This was the initial phase,..but by the time the project had gone into its third phase of suit development and design, the latest Phase III Darktrooper exosuit was classified as a ‘bipedal tank’. Above; General Rom Mohc in his own Phase III Battle suit. General Mohc even had a colossal, customised variant of his own. Not many of these hulking battle suits were produced, but the final glorious result was a mechanical monster, standing at over 2 and a half metres tall. A Stormtrooper to instil dread and fear into the heart of the Rebel Alliance. It boasted an impressive weaponry complement consisting of an overkill arsenal of rocket launchers, missiles, laser canons, frag grenades, thermal detonators and worse. This behemoth became a mobile weapons platform, created by the Empire to eradicate the Rebel pestilence permanently. Above; One Phase III Darktrooper crash landed on Tatooine, and was trapped there for three years, creating havoc for the locals; especially Jabba's swoop gangs. The outer shell of the Darktroopers extremely durable robotic exterior was made from the nearly indestructible material, Phrik, which could withstand a lightsaber strike. Skywalker would have shit his pants after realising his blade was virtually useless against one of these these Imperial wrecking balls. Above; Phase III Battle Suits ready for operation, standing in front of their forebears. Under General Mohcs command a squadron of stormtroopers, decked out with these nightmarish exosuits, slaughtered every single Rebel Alliance member during the bloody massacre of the Attack on Tak Base. Needless to say a high ranking Rebel agent defeated the good general shortly afterwards destroying not only Mohc but a valuable Imperial ship. This incident irrevocably led to the shutdown the Imperial Project, until Moff Gideon and his Imperial scientists discovered the problem with the suit was always the trooper. Below; the attack on Tak Rebel Base by Phase III Darktroopers. Could you just imagine being one of the terrified Rebel troopers at the base, seeing one of these giant mechanoid monstrosities pour out of lingering smoke of your grenade..as you realise that your fate is sealed? The fear, fury and destructive capabilities produced by these revolutionary exosuits makes these guys my pick for favourite Stormtrooper today.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What happened to General Grievous' wife and/or kids in Canon or legends? How was he portrayed as a father (if at all)?
Answer: In Legends General Grievous has a very large family consisting of ten wives and thirty sons and daughters. This is first mentioned in the 2005 James Luceno novel Labyrinth of Evil. When Grievous was known as Qymaen Jai Sheelal there is also the mention of his great grandmother who fought in a great war between their Kaleesh species, and the Bitthaevians at the Invasion of Guetica. She also served alongside a group of Jedi who firstly aligned themselves with Grievous’ people. During the war she used a Czerka Outland Rifle to help liberate her people, and in time this family heirloom was passed down to Grievous’ grandfather who taught the 9 year old Qymaen to become a demigod amongst his people with the weapon. When Qymaen matured and took the name Grievous after losing the love of his life to vicious insectoid invaders known as the Huk, or Yam'rii, he fought a brutal campaign against them and routinely returned home wounded from the battle. In such times Grievous “relied on the support of his wives and children to restore him to life”. It would seem that before the Huk, and the Jedi ripped his heart out Grievous was very family oriented, much like an ancient Viking who would return from voyages and battles to the loving arms of his wife and family. After Grievous was betrayed in a deliberately orchestrated shuttle crash he was given an ultimatum by San Hill of the Intergalactic Banking Clan;..become a cyborg, due to the extent in which his organic body was destroyed, and also become the leader of the droid armies of the Confederacy of Independent Systems. The war that Grievous waged against the Huk drew the attention of the Republic and the Jedi, and after siding with Grievous’ enemies the Jedi imposed harsh sanctions on the planet of Kalee. This cruelly lead many of his wives and children to starve to death and suffer indignitys too depraved to mention,…along with hundreds and thousands of Kaleesh that Grievous swore to avenge. After his shuttle crash San Hill bought in Grievous’ remaining wives and children, and with this the former Kaleesh Warlord took a mask that resembled his fathers death mask,…and began his immense hatred towards the peacekeepers who had willingly doomed his people. After Grievous accepted the offer to lead the droid armies of the CIS his family is never heard from again. Source; General Grievous Wookiepedia, Legends and Canon.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did the Jedi have a division of assassins that operated outside the order, but were still bound by the same principles?
Answer: Well, there were these guys,..and they were actually called The Jedi Assassins in the Expanded Universe fandom. They even had their own Jedi symbol. These mysterious Jedi were carefully selected padawans that were trained in both the lightside..and the darkside of the force, but not known if they were bound by the same principles as the Jedi. Because the Jedi Councils views clashed with using the darkside to fulfil the peaceful purpose set forth by the Jedi, these padawan learners were trained in absolute secrecy. Their existence was only known to a select handful of Jedi. Above; Darth Verraeter. During the time in which the Jedi Assassins operated they were under the threat of the Sith Lord, Darth Verraeter, and covertly trying to sabotage his efforts. The Sith of the era launched terrible attacks on the Republic and the Jedi, and one such incident of the period was the great Battle of Calox III. This battle saw the fall of the Republic, and the Jedi Temple in which the Jedi Assassins were trained. Many were killed by Darth Verraeter himself.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What was the reason behind the Kaminoans creating clone troopers?
Answer: The Kaminoans were businessmen, specialising in making clones. This was what they did. The amphibious locals of Kamino had been pioneers in cloning and genetic engineering, ever since the end of an ice age that forced them to abandon their homes and live in enormous domed cities high above their flooded world. They were known to be extreme isolationists, and kept to themselves, but only to conduct business if it was profitable. They adapted their own genetic code in order to survive the great cataclysm of their world, and in doing so became experts in the field of cloning. They created clones and related technology for various clients across the galaxy, and those that knew of their business ventures, like Dexter Jettster, were aware that you had to be very financially secure to conduct said business with them. After taking the order from the Jedi, for a clone army for the Grand Army of the Republic, the Kaminoans considered the clonetroopers to be their most triumphant achievement. They had recieved the genetic material for the clone template from a bounty hunter named Jango Fett, who had been chosen because of his incredible proficiency in combat and despatching Jedi. After the first 200,000 clones had reached maturity Fett stayed on board with the Kaminoans, and assisted them with training the first generation of ARC troopers at Tipoca City. The Kaminoans played a crucial role in ensuring security for the planets of the Republic with their clone troopers, and recognised that their crowning achievement had been pivotal in opposing the onslaught of the Separatist Alliance. Kamino wasn't the only planet that had clone producing facilities, with a previous facility on Bora Vio being maintained until the major production facility on Kamino was established. The reason behind creating the clonetroopers for the Jedi was strictly business,..until the Empire had no further use for doing business between them; and terminated all existing and future contracts with the Kaminoans.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who is the weakest Sith?
Answer: Maybe not a Sith, but did you catch that Inquisitor that Ahsoka Tano battled in ‘Tales of the Jedi’? This guy had it all going for him; the cool menacing helmet, flames burning poetically in the background, the dark mysterious voice with blazing red eyes, and the cool hooded cape constantly flowing in the wind, but when it came down to business this guy was all talk and no action. We first see this mysterious member of Vaders Inquisitorious in the animated series ‘Tales of the Jedi’, after he locates Ahsoka Tano in hiding..amongst a farming community on a far distant planet. Under the alias Ashla we find Ahsoka hiding out, shortly after attending the funeral for her dear friend Padme. After using the force to save a villager from being crushed, and bringing attention to herself, Ahsoka is ratted out to the Empire by an ambitious and cocky little traitor. After the Inquisitor locates the village where Ahsoka is staying, he murders the innocent townsfolk and sets their peaceful village ablaze. Then when he goes to execute the traitorous informant Ahsoka force grabs his weapon, swiftly takes it off him after he poses some more,..kicks him in the stomach, deactivates his saber..and decapitates him accordingly. This Inquisitor, albeit not a Sith in the traditional sense, was one of the weakest darkside wielders in the saga. The other Inquisitors show some degree of skill throughout Rebels and Kenobi, and even take on opponents like Kanan Jarrus, Ezra Bridger, Maul..and Ahsoka herself. They all put up far better efforts than this postulating, fake Sith,..who cowardly murders a whole village of men woman and children to stroke his ego. Then when it came down to matching blades Ahsoka doesn't even bother wasting time with the fool. She doesn't even use a lightsaber! She just dodges several crap attempts by the Inquisitor to slice her in two, then uses his own blade to swiftly end his life. Strangely though,..when Ahsoka severs his head and it lands on the ground, it turns to mist and evaporates. Canon has his death officially listed at an ‘astronomical object’…and despite his head being removed from his body..this inquisitor might make a comeback in the future, seeing as how his physical body evaporated into the wind. I was just expecting so much more from this guy, but totally let down.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: You come across the humanoids of the Star Wars universe, and they are on average the size of the old action figures (3 inches tall). How do you fare against a fully armed Darth Vader (and you can grab whatever is handy in your household)?
Answer: Wow, for some strange reason this question first reminded of the 1995 movie Indian in the Cupboard. Anyways,..if I encountered an action figure sized, itty bitty Darth Vader in my kitchen then firstly I would be super impressed, and wonder who drugged me,…but after realising that there was a real life, Hasbro sized Sith Lord glaring at me from my countertop..I'd have to act smart..and quick to survive this confusing conundrum. But I don't much like my chances, despite Vader being the size of a couple of Lego dudes. If the question says that I can defend myself with anything in my household then maybe I could fare half decently, especially if I retained some kind of element of suprise. If not then I'm utterly and totally screwed. Yoda was right about size not mattering, because even this little cake topper sized Vader is going to whoop my ass pretty bad. Just think about it; in multiple instances Vader has performed feats like yanking football field sized starships out of the sky, and force crush them until they explode. He didn't care who you were, or how big you were,..and he could even crush your throat via a video call. I might be like the size of a Zillo beast or a Gorax to Darth Kenner, but he's still going to bust me up..and most likely kill me. Even if he didn't use the force he could still drop my ass just by slicing my achilles or tibial nerve, or even slice off all my toes with just one swing. Even at that size Vader could force choke my larynx, or force crush my heart…so the only way I see to outwit the little f@&#er is to maybe entice him into the microwave somehow, just like in Gremlins. I could try and throw him in the juice blender, or bury him in a pot of sand in my backyard, or even swat him like a bug at a picnic, or stomp on him quickly like a spider,..but I own a taser so I'm hoping that will be enough to stop him. It's pretty well just doing the same thing Palps did to him at the end of Return of the Jedi, so here's hoping that my anti-burglar device is enough to stop a less than pint sized Darth Vader. Although, after that..it would be cool to add him to my action figure collection after I miraculously defeated the little guy.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Which Star Wars battle Droid class do you prefer and why?
Answer: I prefer the Droidekas, aka Destroyer Droids. Manufactured by the Colicoid Creation Nest on Colla IV, these rolling, shielded droids were one of the greatest challenges for a Jedi to face during the Clone Wars. At 1.83 meters tall they were an imposing sight on the battlefield, and combined with their two twin blaster cannons proved highly effective against the Jedi and the clones. But their greatest advantage over the enemy was their deflector shield, and the ability to “transform into a ball shape for high speed rolling”. These two features of the Droidekas often made defeating them a near impossible task, until Republic forces worked out that a forward distraction, followed by a rear assault, was effective in destroying the Destroyer Droids. They proved to be one of the CIS's most effective battle droids against the Grand Army of the Republic, and were responsible for thousands of clone casualties during the war. A Droidekas deflector shield, powered by an on board generator, rendered the clones blasters, and the Jedis lightsabers pretty much useless. They had a very furious attitude towards eliminating the enemy with extreme prejudice, which was something that they got from their creators..the vicious Collicoids. I prefer the Droidekas because of their origins. A Droidekas three legged stance is engineered by the Collicoids to resemble their likeness. Standing at over 2 metres tall, and covered in an extremely durable layer of armour the Collicoids were brutal insectoid carnivores from the planet Colla IV, and first began manufacturing the Droidekas for the Trade Federation;.. before ultimately winning the contract with the Confederacy of Independent Systems. The Collicoids were most known throughout the SWU for their “completely emotionless and murderous ways”, and their exotic technology that was mostly foreign to the Republic. They were a very hostile, warmongering species that could roll much like their droid counterpart, and were vicious in their frenzied attacks. When they designed droids in their likeness they had inadvertently created battle droids that would change the war drastically. In exchange for shipments of Droidekas to fuel the Separatist war machine the Collicoids accepted payments in the form of…exotic meats. This must have delighted some of the Neimoidians of the Trade Federation like Nute Gunray, seeing as how he recieved batches of extremely deadly war droids in exchange for some goods from the butcher! Source; Wookiepedia-Droideka, and Collicoids.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How did the Galactic Empire deal with the Umbarans when you consider how formidable they were against the Republic?
Answer: During the Clone Wars the Separatist aligned world of Umbara put up extremely fierce resistance, and proved to the 501st Legion that they weren't a people to be trifled with. Their starships and ground vehicles were revolutionary in design and efficiency, and even considered superior to Republic technology. They utilised a precious metal called Doonium to build their vessels and other technologies. Their reputation became formidable, and they claimed many clones lives in the Battle of Umbara,..which was one of the more bloody and brutal battles of the Clone Wars. But after the demise of the Republic, and the rise of the Empire, everything changed for the Umbarans. During the early days of the Galactic Empire Palpatine dealt with Umbara the same way he dealt with any worlds that opposed his reign;..and swiftly mopped up any pockets of foolish resistance on the planet. Umbara was prized within the Empire because of its vast subterranean mineral wealth, and was pillaged by the Emperor for it accordingly. Ultimately the Galactic Empire imposed a debt on the Umbarans so colossal that they had no choice but to submit, and bow to Palpatine or perish. During this time there was an initial rebellion,..that was quickly suppressed by Captain Thrawn. The Chiss Imperial Captain made an example of the leader of the insurrection, Nevil Cygni. The pirate leader, Nightswan, attempted to take over the mineral wealth of the planet, but Thrawn also shut that down in classic style, and ended any ideas of future insurrections on the shadowy world. During the Imperial reign on Umbara new pockets of Doonium were discovered, which led to the ultimate sell out of the planet. The Mining Guild moved in accordingly after the Imperial contracts were signed,..and then the last remaining wealth on Umbara was greedily exploited and absorbed into Palpatines coffers.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Is the Star Wars character Commander Doom's design based on Marvel’s Doctor Doom?
Answer: Actually..yes, it is! I always wondered this myself over the years, solely based on the name and the green cape synonymous with Marvels supervillain, Dr Doom. Then I did a bit of research and found out that the design for Clone Commander Doom was absolutely based on the MCU Supervillain. For decades now Dr Doom has sported his trademark green cape and outfit, with gold accents, covering his suit of armour. When it came to designing a cool new Clone Commander for Lucas’ The Clone Wars, Dr Dooms outfit design fitted the bill nicely! And so a new Clone Commander was created, and given the nickname ‘Doom’, to pay homage to great and infamous Dr Doom. Clone Commander Doom was introduced in season 6 of TCW, and was present during the Battle of Ringo Vinda, where a preemptive execution of Order 66 lead to the death of his Jedi General Tiplar. Commander Doom, and his men (the doom troopers) are seen battling the Separatist forces of Admiral Trench, and grieving over their fallen commander, as the culprit is questioned by Anakin Skywalker.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What annoys you about the Star Wars sequels?
Answer: One thing that Disney did to the sequel trilogy, that annoyed the crap out of me was the fact that they ditched a load of old alien species that we were all familiar with, and replaced them with their own new aliens and creatures. Maz Kanatas Castle on Tokadana for example is loaded with new alien species to the point where I didn't even recognise a single one! How can we have 6 episodes of the saga lined with alien species that are common in our minds, and then begin the sequel trilogy full of new species we've never seen before. Sure, a few new species here and there wouldn't be uncommon, but if you completely replace them then there's something deeply wrong with the folks who created the sequel trilogy. Take the scenes at the Casino on Canto Bight as another example. As you scan your eyes around the bustling crowd on the casino floor you can't help but notice that they're nearly all new editions to the saga. The only species I thought I could identify was the table attendant, with his tiny little croupiers outfit on, who I first thought was a Zilken like Colonel Meebur Gascon from The Clone Wars,..but as it turned out he was another new addition as well;..a Troglof to be specific. Almost every other character, besides an Ithorian I think I spotted, is of a species unfamiliar to the saga at the time, which to myself doesn't make a lot of sense. Why isn't there one familiar species, besides humans, that we can identify in these two immense scenes full of characters? Don't get me wrong, I enjoy the addition of some of the new alien species and characters, as they continue with the charm of Star Wars and new species being introduced,..but I feel that had Disney included more of the common and familiar species we know then it possibly could have added more value, charm and credibility to the film. Later productions like Solo, Rogue One, The Mandalorian, and Kenobi were more successful in this regard, with the inclusion of species like Twi'leks, Gamorreans, Rodians, Pau’ans, Trandoshans, Ithorians and even Jawas by the truck load. They even had familiar characters and cameos. But in the sequels I feel they went overboard on bringing new too many new species into the saga, without including some of our favourites to add more appeal. Look, my gripe is small compared with most other people's opinions on the sequels;..but I guess when I look at the bigger picture, like killing off my beloved Admiral Ackbar,..and some of the dialogue like “Palpatine somehow returned” didn't do the sequel trilogy justice neither.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What would Anakin do if he crash landed on Earth when slavery was still in practice?
Answer: Let's say Anakin Skywalker flew through a dimensional rift, and ended up crashing near the Great Pyramids of Giza,..nearly two and a half thousand years ago. What would he make of this situation you ask? Firstly R2-D2 would eject from the Jedi Starfighter and do a diagnostic sweep of the immediate area. Determining very little threat from this primitive species he would proceed to make repairs to his masters ticket off this backwater world. Meanwhile,..Anakin investigates the gold clad locals, rocking up on some sort of primitive chariot. Viewing his desert surroundings, very reminiscent to him of Tatooine..and his time as a boy.., he immediately determines that he is witnessing an army of slaves being put to work. Memories of the Zygerrian Empires cruel slavery legacy, from his own galaxy, would come flooding back;..and the memories of himself and his mother as slaves to the Hutts. The pyramid structures that are reminiscent of Zygerrian culture, the guards whipping and subjugating the slaves, and the cruel, opulent overseers barking orders and holding innocents against their will. Snap. R2-D2 gives the signal that it was a minor crash, and the little repairs needed to be done are already finished. Anakin briefly acknowledges his faithful astromech, as he sums up the situation in his head. As the first group of the Pharaoh's guards roll up, and begin to whip the astonished slaves milling around Skywalker, the Jedi force grabs the cruel guards and sends them hurtling off somewhere beyond the dunes. R2 fires up the Aethersprite and prepares to take off. Anakin stands on the bow of the ship, as he notices more chariots, more guards and what looked like their pompous rulers in a carriage, slowly coming down the pillared road. “Take me up Artoo!” As he beckons his droid to lift the ship up, and stop as he reaches the height of the great edifice, he uses the loudspeakers on the Jedi starfighter to announce his departure. “Citizens of this land..” He shouts, as he raises his hands in the air and gestures them in a choking manner.. “You are now free!“ Then, as the Pharaoh and all his bodyguards arrive beneath his floating starship,..Anakin Skywalker closes his fists and simultaneously crushes each and every last one of their larynxes. Baring witness to all of this the frightened slaves huddle in silent astonishment. Those few guards who are spared his wrath flee like rats, screaming into the desert wastes,…as a joyous roar of liberation erupts from the thousands of slaves surrounding the giant pyramid. “Take us home Artoo.” Says Skywalker, as he drops into his pilots seat.. and gives a little smirk of smug satisfaction. . . . Meanwhile back on Earth..in 1940s Nazi occupied Egypt, a bold archaeologist makes a startling discovery...

Name: John Bambrook
Question: If you can make a base in Star Wars, where would you build it? What equipment would you have? What starfighters would you use?
Answer: The perfect base already exists, so I wouldn't have to build it,…and it was personally designed to keep people out, and also to prevent people from ever leaving alive. This base was once owned by one of the most fearsome entities in the entire galaxy, and served as his hidden fortress; complete with booby traps and a massive ‘guard dog’ named Gor. Built into the rockface of a deep, expansive gorge and surrounded in fog this impressive castle could serve me as a base, a fortress..and a very impressive home to boast about. On the third moon of the planet Vassek lays a massive, concealed fortress, completely shrouded in fog and nearly undetectable to the naked eye. This enormous, ominous looking castle was once home to the infamous Separatist leader General Grievous. It would make for a perfect, hidden base…and is already stocked with equipment that would suffice. Grievous had a complement of IG-100 Magnaguards, which if equipped with T-7 Ion Disruptors would make for excellent sentries. Of course I'd have to beef up the already bolstered security measures, which already included a molten incinerator trap hidden beneath the floor, and other various concealed traps. It also had a central control room to keep everything in check. As for my starfighter, well..Grievous had a custom Bellbulab-22 Heavy Starfighter, manufactured by Feethan Ottraw Scaleable Assemblies, dubbed Soulless One. This impressive vessel boasted Triple Rapid fire laser cannons and was coated in Impervium. If modified correctly, its armaments were improved and it's Class 2 Hyperdrive was upgraded, it would serve as a perfect Starfighter, to complement my perfect base. Plus Grievous had some classy garden statues going on at his place which added that “homely” appeal, so a few indoor plants, some mood lighting, and maybe a fountain would spruce the old place up.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Do you think Owen and Beru Lars will be confronted by an inquisitor in the Kenobi series?
Answer: Yes. At some point in time I believe curiosity got the better of Vader, and eventually he despatched one or more of his Imperial Inquisitors to Tatooine, to spy on his late step father's house near Mos Eisley. Whether it was the force whispering something to him, or whether it was out of a twisted sense of ‘checking up’ on the only family he thought he had left..at some point after the Empire seized power he had to know what the Lars couple had been doing all these years. I think it might play out something like in the 2005 Star Wars graphic novel ‘Visionaries’. Seeing as how geniuses like Jon Favreau, of The Mandalorian fame, are incorporating elements of the Expanded Universe into current Canon, I think they might be heavily inspired by events that happened in this old EU comic. In the story Maul comes to Tatooine and attempts to attack the Lars homestead, knocking Owen Lars temporarily unconscious. Then Kenobi springs from the sand, where he had been hiding in anticipation of Mauls attack, and confronts his old nemesis. I believe that in the upcoming Kenobi series it won't be Maul coming to the Lars homestead, because his canon story arc ends differently with Kenobi, but instead it will be one of the members of the Imperial Inquisitorious. Undoubtedly the Inquisitor will confront Owen and Beru, possibly about a ‘force sensitive child’, but how Kenobi deals with him/her remains the mystery.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Is it possible for Yoda to defeat General Grievous without using his lightsaber?
Answer: Yes. If General Grievous was fully armed, spinning his four lightsabers..coming at Yoda with the full intent on eviscerating him..then I strongly believe that Master Yoda would defeat the good general within moments of engaging him. Yoda was no fool, and recognised General Grievous for what he was. He was completely aware that the general only wielded Jedi weapons, and did not possess a Jedis connection to the force. This actually made Grievous weaker in Yodas mind, and there would have been more than a few ways that Yoda could have dealt with the wayward warrior. Yodas greatest weapon was his ability to use the force in grandiose style. He could levitate X-Wings from swamps, send massive stone slabs flying and completely freeze an individual to the spot using force grab. General Grievous can rant and rave all he wants, and unleash a terrible fury that few Jedi could withstand: but Yoda isn't going to entertain the generals posturing. To defeat General Grievous without a lightsaber would be relatively easy for Grievous, as Grand Master Yoda can just hold and suspend the general in mid air…and decide his fate on a whim. He could just force crush him with a wave of his wrist, or unleash electric judgement and fry his cybernetic circuits. Or just suspend Grievous to the floor, and use the force to levitate his lightsaber up to the generals neck, and…

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who would win in a fight between Darth Vader and Kylo Ren? How close would the fight be?
Answer: How close would the fight be? Surely you jest,..as the closeness of this fight would be as far as from one end of an Imperial Star Destroyer to the other! If we put aside the family feelings and just focus on each opponents strong sides Vader categorically beats his grandson on nearly every matchup. Speed and agility is about the only thing young Kylo has going for him here, because his infamous grandfather trumps everything else from strength, durability, resiliency, and sheer focus and depth in the darkside. Ren idolised his grandfather for obvious reasons;..because he was a god compared to himself. But remember the way he reacted to Rey Palpatine telling him that he was afraid;..afraid he could never be as powerful as Darth Vader? That's the difference between these two; Kylo Ren had too many conflicting emotions swirling around in his head, with fear being the most prominent. Vader did not. Vader embraced fear and basically fed off it. He was disciplined, extremely focused and despite being a little petulant, not a candle compared to Rens cock-blocked teenage outbursts. Vaders feats were legendary in comparison to Rens, despite the latter being able to bring down a mighty Zillo Beast in the comics. Vader did the same and more though, being capable of plucking massive vessels from orbit, surviving the molten hot lava of Mustafar, single handedly taking on entire platoons of the enemy, killing a Summa Verminoth, taking on Palpatine himself, and more importantly..killing Jedi. Vader was a Jedi killing nightmare and his skills in the force, both before and after falling to the darkside,..towered far above the meager talents of an angsty young boy. Disgraced former Jedi, Kazdan Paratus would have had a better chance at defeating Vader than Ren, and that cowardly little Aleena ran away from the Jedi Temple during Order 66! Vader was the chosen one, created by the force itself to bring balance back to it, and he was driven by pure rage, fury…and an anger the likes Kylo could only dream of possessing. He was a true Sith Lord, trained by the most powerful being in the entire galaxy. Ren was taught by a puppet of Palpatines own devising. I imagine if Kylo Ren could actually stand before his grandfather Vaders presence alone would be enough to instil more fear, and awe than Ren thought possible. This fight isn't even close enough to call a contest, with Vader uttering one last badass one liner.. before putting an end to Ben Solo. Never send a Knight to take out a God.

Question: Is the TIE bomber considered a variant of the TIE Fighter or are they separate ships altogether? What is the difference besides TIE bombers having the ability to drop explosives and different wing designs?
Answer: The TIE/sa Bomber is a variant of the TIE Fighter. Designed by the same manufacturer, Seinar Fleet Systems, the TIE Bomber boasts the same Twin Ion Engines as the standard TIE/LN Fighter. It is slightly longer at 7.8 metres, over the TIE fighters 7.2 metres. A standard TIE Fighter is 8.8 metres tall, and the Bomber is 5.1 metres. It is slower at 850kph, under the TIE Fighters 1200kph, and has no shields or hyperdrive like its counterpart, but does have onboard life support. It did have inclined wings, much the same as the TIE Advanced, which gave it better manoeuvrability whilst carrying heavy ordnance into situations. It's main distinguishing feature, that set it apart from a regular TIE was its iconic twin operational pods, which had one for the pilot, and the other for bombing ordnance; complete with a bomb chute connected to the on board targeting systems. In addition to its various bombs, concussion missiles and proton torpedoes the craft was also equipped with homing missiles and twin laser cannons. They could be fitted for various roles in their anti-emplacement anti-trap air support positions. These bombers were usually deployed to carpet bomb the enemy and weaken its infrastructure, and they could even be fitted to carry up to six stormtroopers for rapid deployment. Source; Wookiepedia- TIE/sa Bomber and TIE/LN Fighter.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is something about Star Wars that always irked you?
Answer: Yodas lightsaber. Not the lightsaber itself, but the glaring discrepancy of continuity pertaining to its fate. After Yoda has his epic duel with Palpatine in the Senate Building his lightsaber was lost during the battle. This was 2002. Now here's where it gets a little hazy, until Grogu refuses it from Luke Skywalker in chapter 6 of The Book of Boba Fett. After the duel in the Senate Building it was stated that in Star Wars:Complete Locations, 2016, that somehow it ended up being stored in a box in Yodas hut on Dagobah. This is by the time the events of The Empire Strikes Back commence. But then a year later in 2017, the Darth Vader #1 comic shows it being destroyed in a ceremony officiated by Mas Amedda, with Palpatine and Vader watching from above. This is when it was stated by Lucasfilm that Yoda probably had a few lightsabers in his time,.. …and then to put an end to the long standing discrepancy they try to end it five years later in the comic Crimson Reign, issue #3. Here it is ultimately stated that it is was only “one” of Yodas lightsabers that was destroyed by Mas Amedda in the lightsaber burning ceremony of '17. Yodas lightsaber was very first introduced in 1999s Episode I, Visual dictionary,..then we see Yoda use it in Episode II against Dooku,..then it takes well over two decades for its fate to be definitively ascertained. Even then, the lightsaber that Luke offers Grogu is just his second one, and not the one from Revenge of the Sith. This just irks me because of how long it took to be rectified,..and now people can just... ”Oh,..do you know how Maz Kanata got one of Luke Skywalkers lightsabers in The Force Awakens?”

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Do the stun batons in the new Star Wars movies (and JFO) block lightsabers because of some special material in them, or is it just the electricity?
Answer: Upon further inspection it is only the powerful electrical current that enables the Z-76 Riot Control Baton to block a lightsaber. Seen in debut film of the sequel trilogy, The Force Awakens, and manufactured by the First Order to be utilised in their non lethal weapons program, the Z-76s prime function was to “batter their opponents into submission.” The two long contact conductor vanes, which were connected by the central shaft, were made of alloys that a lightsaber blade could easily cut in two given enough exposure. Its handle had an inbuilt adhesion grip that magnomatomically paired with the Riot troopers gloves. Once activated the Z-76 delivered a powerful charge capable of withstanding the plasma blade of a lightsaber. The conductor vane was useless against a lightsaber by itself. The vanes only acted as a wide surface area for the electrical charge to spread along. The Purge Troopers from Jedi: Fallen Order are equipped with similar weapons to allow them to take on the Jedi. These troopers used a variety of stun weaponry including electobatons, electrostaffs and electrohammers, however unlike the First Orders batons the Purge Troopers weapons were highly lethal; just like Grievous’ Magnaguards weapons, which could also block lightsabers, and stop the heart with enough charge. The Electrohammer could be charged up and slammed into the ground, creating a devastating shock wave that sent opponents flying, or if it was angled could create a ripple capable of knocking any Jedi off their feet.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: If General Grievous could use the Force, would it have been a game changer in The Clone Wars?
Answer: If General Grievous could use the force then Obi-Wan Kenobi would most likely have died in the first year of the Clone Wars. It wouldn't just be a game changer, but could possibly be the game changer. In Legends Count Dooku gives his general a blood transfusion from the late Jedi Master Sifo Dyas. Now let's say that this transfusion worked and enabled Grievous to use the force. What now? Depending on circumstances if Grievous kept this little secret to himself then he could possibly add even more lightsabers to his growing collection. Imagine all those times when Grievous scuttled away from a duel,..and now imagine those times if Grievous could use the force! Jedi like Mace Windu, Kit Fisto and Kenobi himself could all have fallen to his blades, and countless more soldiers, vehicles and ships would have followed. Grievous was already proficient in lightsaber combat, and already a highly skilled opponent for any Jedi. If the cybernetic Kaleesh Warlord could wield the force then all it would do is make him more lethally efficient, and fuel his new murderous appetite. Grievous accepted his ‘modifications’ in a bid to destroy the Jedi, but now he can wield the force he is instantly better than a large chunk of the Order. It's rare for a Jedi to be proficient in all 7 forms of lightsaber combat, but Dooku instructed Grievous in all of them. That makes him better than a large chunk of the remainder of the Order now. Up until the breakout of the Clone Wars the Jedi had spent a millenia as peacekeepers, instead of war generals. Grievous had spent his whole life in combat as it made him the tactical genius that he was. The Jedi had to acclimate to their roles on the battlefield, whereas Grievous relished at the opportunity to lead the charge. If you consider all the aforementioned factors, and now reset them to account for the fact that the general is now evenly matched for most Jedi,..then I'd call that a game changer. Now Grievous is going to wait until he is up close and personal with the first Jedi he encounters, and unbeknownst to the Jedi Grievous can now force choke him, force crush his lungs, and force throw he or she straight into a solid duranium wall. The odds have turned against the Jedi severely, and because of the force Grievous can not only kill the Jedi with his lightsabers…but practically force pull his opponents towards him and into his swirling sabers of oblivion. His lightsaber collection at this point would even make Professor Huyang blush.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Do Battle Droids have emotions?
Answer: You just have to see a couple of episodes of The Clone Wars to see that some battle droids of the Separatist Alliance have slight personalities, that set them apart from almost all the other mindless minions in the droid armies. Not so much with the B2 Battle Droids, but the later versions of the B1 expressed some suprising emotions. If you look at the above scene, particularly the two B1 battle droids standing in between Kenobi and Grievous, just off in the distance. The droid on the right motions to his companion to watch their general take out his lightsabers. On this occasion the droid was trying to convey a “Wait for it” kinda feeling as he anticipated the excitement. Here we have the Battle Droids in the Geonosian arena, as they surround the Jedi. This B2 expresses frustration at one of his lesser counterparts getting in his way. It's almost as if that B1 genuinely angered him, giving the abrupt, violent way he hurled him aside. The B1 was shot a moment before the punishment from the B2, possibly meaning their programming here accounted for damaged and useless companions. Trash them and press forward. The above two droids here express shock and disbelief upon surviving a blast, and even check themselves to see if they were damaged. They even look genuinely astonished that they didn't lose a limb or something, despite being unable to express emotion on their faces. Above, this B1 gives a brief explanation as to why some droids were more independent. When we watch The Phantom Menace we see that when Anakin destroys the Separatist Control vessel he also destroyed the central computer, thus shutting down the droids who were remotely attached to it. Later models of the B1 were designed to operate more independently, without requiring the assistance of a central computer to program their orders. This allowed them to be more animated in their responses and actions, giving them a more emotional quality. The Clone Wars is the franchises best example to witness their emotional displays. Here a droid meets Wrecker from the Bad Batch, and right before the enormous clone pummels the poor droid into the floor the B1 expresses fear, particularly at the prospect of having his face messed up. The droid below even tries to warn his boss about an impending attack from non other than…Kenobi. He conveyed suprise and emergency with his tone, and sounded worried about Grievous possibly being attacked by the insolent Jedi. Below is where some droids are cornered by Skywalker, and upon realising that their fates are sealed resign themselves to the Jedi’s swing. The one on the right slouches his shoulders in defeat, as if he had seen Skywalkers fury firsthand. The other one still wanted to put up a fight, meaning there were conflicting emotions amongst themselves. It's rather sad how something programmed,..hard and cold, can express so much emotion just from some small body language. Finally, here's some more Battle Droid images, because I know that some of you out there are big fans of those B1’s! Roger Roger.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How was Vader able to choke out Admiral Ozzel through a monitor?
Answer: Because a Sith doesn't need to be in the same location as someone in order to force choke them. On several occasions throughout the clone wars we see that a force user doesn't need to be in the same vicinity as their target, or even on the same planet, to execute a force choke. So long as the user has an exact location of the target they can perform this move, especially if they are strong in the force. We witnessed this in The Clone Wars when we see Count Dooku getting force choked by his master Darth Sidious. Dooku was at his personal palace on Serenno, and presumably Sidious was back on Coruscant. These two planets are many light years apart, and would take many hours to travel to, even using light engines. The power of the darkside is very potent, with a very wide reach. When Vader was force choking Ozzel, Vader was aboard the same Star Destroyer as the incompetent Admiral. Once Vader ascertained Ozzels position distance became irrelevant, and Vader reached out through the force to reprimand his pompous officer. Vader also liked making very public examples of his foolish subordinates, and through the view screen he could inspire the next officer in line after Ozzel. This was just another one of Darth Vaders ways to instil terror, establish dominance and hopefully inspire leadership and determination. Force choking the former Admiral served its purpose, and let all aboard the same vessel know the price for failure.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who did you find to be the most annoying character or creatures in the Star Wars Canon and why?
Answer: Jawas. Always with the Jawas. It doesn't matter if you find them on Tatooine, Nevarro or Arvala-7..as they're always swindling, or straight up ripping off folks. Yes, they have their talents, particularly when it comes to “acquiring” that rare or extremely hard to find piece of hardware..but at what cost? They'll probably steal from your neighbour, sell you the part, and create mixed feelings about the whole transaction. We first see their rip off tactics in A New Hope, where Owen Lars gets sold a droid with a bad motivator,..and the method for acquiring these droids is just straight up theft. They fried R2-D2s circuits out in the wastes of Tatooine, kidnapped him, and promptly sold him to the next sucker in line, (being Owen Lars). Din Djarin had his unfortunate encounter with these thieves when he was pulling a job off on Arvalo-7, and after leaving his Razor Crest parked he returned to find it stripped almost completely bare!! Then to get his parts back the Jawas had the nerve to make Din go and get dirty, and almost get killed, retrieving an enormous Mud Horns filthy egg. Obi-Wan Kenobi would also have to deal with shifty little Jawas, whereupon relocating to Tatooine one particular Jawa, Teeka, would steal Kenobi's items, then sell them back to him. It was just something that Kenobi had to accept if he wanted to keep getting items he desperately needed, because the damn Jawas completely cornered the market on most technical items on Tatooine. On top of all of this they apparently smelt really bad up close..and sometimes get extremely sarcastic during barters. Gamorreans and Gungans might be clumsy, lazy and inept simpletons, but they won't steal your parts and sell them to your neighbours.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Do swords exist in Star Wars?
Answer: Of course they do. What do you think that the Jedi based their lightsabers on? They do refer to it as a “laser sword” in the Star Wars Universe. Many thousands of primitive or rudimentary planets still employed the use of swords, and many species still took pride in crafting these ancient yet effective weapons. Twi'leks, Kaleesh, Kyuzo, Dathomirians, Nightsisters, Mandalorians and other cultures still use swords in combat occasionally, while keeping ceremonial swords and daggers as reminders of their people's past. Above; a pre-cyborg General Grievous The Kaleesh are a very warlike and Spartan culture, who still use swords, spears and daggers as weapons of war. Before he brandished quadruple lightsabers, and became a psychopathic cyborg, General Grievous used swords to vanquish his enemies, such as the Huk species, who had invaded and enslaved Kallee. As a Warlord, back on Kallee, he used to behead his opponents with his blood stained sword. Below; Qymaen Jai Shelal beheads his enemy. The Toydarian people have curved bladed swords, that are still carried as weapons, and their ruler, King Katuunko, had a beautiful custom one of his own. Below; King Katuunko, the Toydarian ruler, brandishes a Ceremonial sword. The Kage warriors use ancient electro swords to engage their enemy the Belugans, and even the Sith are partial to brandishing a sword from time to time. Above; Naga Sadow and Ludo Kressh duel with dark imbued Sith Swords. Ludo Kressh preferred to use a sword, rather than a lightsaber, and his Sith imbued sword was an extremely deadly, double edged weapon. Another Sith Lord, Naga Sadow, used a Sith sword, which he actually fought Ludo Kressh with, and the Dathomirian Nightsister leader, Mother Talzin, could conjure a dark imbued sword out of thin air. Below; Mother Talzin conjures a Nightsister sword.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What has Disney done right with the Mandalorian that they haven't done in the movies?
Answer: I'll assume you're referring to the sequel trilogy when you say “movies”. What The Mandalorian, or more importantly Disney, have done right is pretty much everything compared to what they served up with those other ‘movies’. The sequel trilogy was set 30+ years after Return of the Jedi, and this detracts from everyone's memory of that good old fashioned ‘Star Wars feeling’. It introduced a plethora of new aliens, planets and characters that weren't well received by audiences, whereas in The Mandalorian, the story is set less than half a decade after the destruction of the second Death Star in ROTJ. The galaxy in Favreaus show was dirty, grimy, old and worn. It felt like a really bigass, real SW movie, which was in stark contrast with the shiny, sterile environment of the sequels. The comedy factor in The Mandalorian shat all over the wooden, hollow performances in the new ‘movies’. As for the lead role characters in both The Mandalorian and the sequel trilogy, the latter missed the mark by introducing overkill, no training, whiny Mary Sues for lead roles,..and killed off Han Solo, Leia, Luke friggin Skywalker,..and a couple of other beloved characters such as Admiral Ackbar. This disappointed me more than words can express..but in The Mandalorian the characters in the galaxy are familiar and fresh in our minds. Ahsoka, Bo Katan, Boba Fett, Luke Skywalker and more, transport us straight back into the story because they are familiar with us. Rey, Kylo and the gang just missed the mark, and as new characters copped a lot of criticism and backlash. They lacked character development, but in The Mandalorian the characters were either established, or had incredible character development. Din Djarin went straight up John Wick at some points, whereas Rey just… Lots of people are tired of the whole ‘Skywalker angle’, but The Mandalorian incorporated the Skywalker legacy with a whole new story, lead protagonist, but familiar locations and characters. The Empire was familiar, whereas The First Order was received in translation as a sloppy copy of its predecessor. Its things like this that detract from the main story being told in the sequel trilogy, whereas in The Mandalorian we can kick back, and enjoy relatable characters, in a familiar setting. The plot comparisons in each were vastly different also. Din Djarins quest to return Grogu to the Jedi, and all that it entailed, made for a much enjoyable viewing experience than that shipwreck of a plot from the entire sequel trilogy.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Could the Sith troopers in TROS be clones?
Answer: The Sith Troopers were not clones. When the Empire came to an end after Operation Cinder the remnants of the Imperial officers and stormtroopers went to live on Exegol. Palpatines plan was to revive his Empire hidden away on the shady planet. The Sith Troopers were children of the Empire, and also children from the Sith Eternal occultists who already resided on Exegol. The planet was safely hidden in the Unknown Regions of space, and virtually impossible for anyone to locate without a Sith Wayfinder. The children of these two factions would go on to becoming the Sith Troopers. While they had no connection to the force they were completely loyal to the Sith, and to Palpatine. Because the Sith occultists ruled the planet of Exegol Palpatine had thousands upon thousands of children to conscript into his Final Order. The children were raised to worship the Sith, and to be diehards fanatical to Palpatines cause. Their devotion to Palpatine was without question, unwavering and totally loyal,..unlike the officers and troops of the Empire and First Order. Both respectively didn't rely on clones, and neither did Palpatines Final Order and the Sith Troopers. Instead Palpatine refined the work of the Kaminoan scientists pertaining to brain conditioning, and through the use of these techniques they managed to totally suppress the free will of the Sith Troopers. Palpatine did this via way of.. Because Palpatine finally worked out how to completely control his troops through brain manipulation he didn't need to use clones. His former Imperial staff, and the Sith Occultists, would provide him with enough soldiers, and through the work of his own scientists and the legacy of the Kaminoans he had an army unquestionably loyal to him. Source; Sith troopers:Wookiepedia

Name: John Bambrook
Question: If Leia was forced to smoke Jabba's hookah, would she enjoy it? If not, why?
Answer: If she was forced to smoke Jabbas grandiose hookah pipe then I'm fairly certain she isn't going to fondly remember the experience any time in the near future. Jabba made a very lucrative profit from dealing and running Spice throughout the galaxy, especially through the use of smugglers, like Han Solo and Chewbacca among others. Jabba also liked to participate in the smoking of spice, and the SWU's version of tobacco, simply called t'bac. But like Lom Pyke of the Pyke Syndicate Jabba also liked to “get high on his own supply”, and in the safety of his palace he would smoke his hookah, and snack on his Klatooine Paddy frogs that were stored in the lower portion of his impressive looking smoking apparatus. Princess Leia was definitely not like Jabba the Hutt, and certainly would not enjoy it. Leia was raised by Alderaan nobility, and as a princess wouldn't be seen dead smoking from a filthy Hutt hookah. Sansanna spice was one of the more potent and addictive strains of the illegal narcotic, and Leias royal upbringing would leave her with mixed negative emotions after the whole ordeal. Such potent spice would dramatically affect her judgement, and produce behaviour very unbefitting of a princess; and she would be absolutely wigging out on sounds and lights after smoking Jabbas curious hallucinigentics. Imagine being imprisoned by a murderous Hutt gangster, made to wear some cheap, skimpy attire while hordes of prying eyes leer at you,…and then being forced by the crimelord to smoke spice from his saliva soaked bong! No,..no one would like to smoke from Jabbas disgusting hookah, especially after it looks like he's eating the Paddy Frogs from the dirty bong water. Yeeech!!

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why does it seem like Star Wars clone troopers with black hair are the unluckiest ones?
Answer: What the heck are you talking about? Every single clone manufactured by their Kaminoan creators had black hair! Jango Fett, as we all know, was the template for every single clone trooper in the Grand Army of the Republic, and he had black hair from birth. The Kaminoans sure as hell didn't care about the clones hair colour, and neither did the Jedi. Clones such as Captain Rex, Commander Gree and Crys, had different coloured hair, which they would have dyed and styled themselves. This was done to create an individual look to accompany their individual personalities. Gree rocked the double red stripe, and Rex had a short cropped, blonde hair style. As I said, this was an individual choice for clones to colour their hair,..but at the end of the day each and every single clone trooper was born with black hair. Commander Gree may have been wearing a different hairstyle than most of his brethren,..but he still lost his head when carrying out Order 66.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is a Force saber in Star Wars?
Answer: A Force saber was a Rakatan invention which predates the Jedis lightsaber by thousands of years. It was created many millenia before 36,000 BBY, was constructed using a metal hilt and powered by an Ebon crystal. These vicious melee weapons were actually powered by the darkside of the force, which the Rakatan Force Hounds channelled into the Ebon crystals, giving the blades their tremendous power. The ancient Rakatan grew these crystals in their laboratories, and used the force sensitive individuals called Force Hounds to craft the eerie glowing weapons using a form of arcane force Alchemy. You could say that the Rakatan Empire was literally light years ahead of the Jedi when it came to developing each cultures most prominent weapon of choice. When they were created they could resemble a regular lightsaber, or force pike like the one Darth Plagueis wielded. The most interesting thing about the Force saber was the fact, that in Legends lore, it was considered to be the number one catalyst that created the divide between the dark and light sides of the force. Legend has it that because the Force saber drew its power from the darkside, it greatly affected whoever wielded the weapon. When the Rakata began waging war against the Je'daii many from the Order wished to carry the weapons themselves, given the great power they provided in resisting Rakatan attacks. Many Jedi were against this proposal,..hence leading to the beginning of the great divide. Source; Wookiepedia, and Force saber first seen in 2012 comic series ‘Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm’.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why could clone troopers shoot Jedi but battle droids could not?
Answer: Quality,..not quantity. That's why. The clonetroopers of the Grand Army of the Republic were all cloned from the number one bounty hunter of his day, Jango Fett. Fetts impressive DNA, coupled with his lifetime of extensive training and experience, resulted in the clones becoming far more accurate than most fighting forces within the SWU. Count Dooku carefully selected the clone template candidate based on his abilities to kill Jedi. When Jango was still perfecting his skills he single handedly took out 6 Jedi during the Battle of Galidraan, which Dooku witnessed first hand. That fateful day the Count bore witness to the man who would ultimately become the face of the Republics impressive new army. The Kaminoans also used Jango to assist hands on in the training of new clones, giving them a far more lethal edge in combat..as opposed to the droids of the CIS. Every Alpha class ARC Trooper also went through extensive one on one training with Jango himself. So when the time finally arrived to execute Order 66 the clones were very well equipped to decimate the Jedi Order. Unlike the Stormtroopers of the Galactic Empire all of the clonetroopers had superior fighting blood coursing through their veins. However the droid armies of the Separatist Alliance were limited by their programming, which wasn't up to the high calibre of the clones physical training,..and so the droids blaster combat, and manoeuvrability skills, were simply no match for the clones lethal accuracy. The droids greatest advantage lay in their vast numbers, which were usually used to overwhelm the Republic forces en masse. This method was first displayed when Dooku's droids surrounded, then massacred most of the Jedi in the Geonosian arena. By swarming their enemy with outnumbered odds the Separatist Alliance were able to achieve victories, but had the odds been even for every single engagement the Republic had with the CIS then the clones would mop up the droids. Order 66 worked a lot like a Separatist droid attack during the Clone Wars. The soldiers of the 501st overwhelmed the Jedi Temple, but also retained the element of suprise..up until the first shots of the great Jedi Purge echoed throughout the hallways and rooms of the great temple. Their home ultimately became their tomb, at the hands of their former comrades in arms.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why does the seventh sister have such a unique voice, even slightly electronic?
Answer: Every Jedi who was inducted into the Imperial Inquisitorious was personally taught the lesson of loss..at the hand of Darth Vader himself. Now that may have included losing a limb, or being bisected! Vader was utterly merciless as he taught the inductees to fully respect the value of loss,.. and use the tremendous anger and pain that it generated to make them even more powerful darkside adepts. Each Inquisitors outfit was all black leather and fancy padding, so it was hard to tell if the Seventh Sister had lost a limb;..but she was one really intriguing customer. She did have an electronically enhanced voice when she has her mask on..but still an echo of it persists after it is removed. My suspicion was that during her day, that Vader instructed the lesson of loss to her, she may have gotten a bit too lippy with her new darklord overseer...and Vader possibly crushed her larynx or something equally appropriate. She could have suffered a neck or throat injury, requiring the permanent use of an electronic vocabulator, or she might even have been mute from birth..and taught to speak through the use of a voice enhancer. We just don't know the definitive reason behind why her voice is slightly electronically manipulated. Or..it might be because of the fact that the ageless Sarah Michelle Gellar, the actress who voiced the Seventh Sister, is married in real life to Freddie Prinze Jr, who voiced Kanan Jarrus in Rebels animated. Now when they confront one another in the series it might sound a bit like a lovers quarrel, or an old married couple arguing about something,..just totally detracting from the story being told; y'know..just give her voice that cold, mechanical tone to let you know who actually wears the pants around here.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, how do ship-based cloaking devices work?
Answer: Cloaking devices in the Star Wars Universe are extremely rare, and operated by utilising the even rarer stygium crystals. These crystals were mined on the volcanic and unstable planet of Aeten II. In Legends lore the planet was destroyed in 3 ABY, not long after the Battle of Hoth, but by then it had already stated that the stygium mines had nearly ran dry. But in Canon the planet fell under the control of the Empire, and more than likely a similar scenario occurred. Either way, the crystals that powered the cloaking devices became rarer and rarer, rendering stealth technology such as this very hard to acquire or maintain. When Darth Maul served under Darth Sidious he was given the Scimitar, which is stated was canonically built by Sienar Design Systems, and later customized in an unknown laboratory. The cloaking system operates on the premise of using the power from more than 30 stygium crystals, ran through a ‘Cloak Field Generator’, and then the field that was created from this process was used to envelope the star courier in an invisible field. It was regulated through an overload cache, located in the middle of each of its wings, and the process made possible by the stygium crystals blocked every pursuing crafts scanners. However, it could still be tracked via its magnetic signature. The Scimitar itself was also canonically stated to be able to track another vessels signature through hyperspace. After Maul supposedly perished on Naboo the Scimitar fell back into possession of Darth Sidious. It was used by himself and General Grievous to arrive on Dathomir unseen, as Sidious hunted and killed the witch Mother Talzin. Above; Xanadu Blood, Cad Banes Porax-38, Rogue Class Starfighter. During the Clone Wars Darth Sidious gifted a cloaked ship, a Rogue Class Porax-38 Starfighter named Xanadu Blood, to the bounty hunter Cad Bane as payment for his outstanding services. Above; the Republic stealth ship, the IPV-2C. During the Clone Wars the Republic developed a cloaked vessel, the IPV-2C Stealth Corvette, that they used to elude and defeat the forces of Separatist Commander, Admiral Trench; and later Grand Moff Wilhuff Tarkin used a cloaked vessel named The Carrion Spike, that was designed from the original Stealth Corvette. Below; Grand Moff Tarkins personal stealth ship, the Carrion Spike. In the reference book, Incredible Cross Sections: Episode I, it states.. “An invisibility field is a terrifying weapon, since it can detect most security systems and make acts of theft, sabotage and assassination all but unstoppable.”

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What smallest and biggest change in Star Wars would have changed the entire stories outcome?
Answer: If R5-D4, from the beginning of A New Hope, never fried his motivator then the entire original trilogy simply wouldn't have happened. R2-D2 wouldn't have taken his place, delivered Princess Leias message and the plans of the Death Star to Kenobi. Luke stays on at his Uncles moisture farm for more than “just one more season”, Princess Leia is tried for treason against the Empire, which is just another way of saying “Tarkin has her executed, and then blows up Alderaan and Yavin IV”. This destroys most of the Rebel Alliance, leaving the Empire to crush the last resistance to their absolute rule over the galaxy. This is just one small change that would have completely affected the outcome of the OT, but what are some more examples. Imagine if Phoenix Squadron never took Ezra in,..or if Luke never managed to free his lightsaber from the ice on Hoth. Imagine what would have happened if Palpatine somehow didn't return, or if Rey never bypassed the compressor; or if Ben Solo returned to the light, and never killed his father Han Solo. Or even think of the outcome if Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan were never forced to land on Tatooine,..or if Palpatine was never elected into the office of Supreme Chancellor. What would have happened if Din Djarin never had a conscience on Nevarro, after delivery Grogu to the client, or if Luke never made his “one in a million” shot on the Death Star. What would have happened if Wookiees were used on Endor, or if Qui-Gon killed Darth Maul…or if Mother Talzin actually killed Dooku using Nightsister magicks? Imagine the outcome if Anakin got the high ground on Mustafar,..or if General Grievous got the low ground on Utapauu.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Do you think Darth Vader is the best pilot in the Galaxy?
Answer: Without a doubt! As Anakin Skywalker he was widely known amongst the Jedi to be the greatest starship pilot in the Order, but then after his transformation into Darth Vader I believe he was an even more deadlier and proficient pilot than before. In Rebels animated, during the ‘Seige of Lothal’, Vader singlehandedly takes on the Rebel cell Phoenix Squadron,..and hands their asses back to them in a little velvet lined box. Vader exhibits amazing prowess as a pilot, as he manoeuvres his TIE Advanced X1 with devastatingly lethal effect. Using the force, coupled with his natural piloting abilities, Vader cuts through the Rebels with ease, decimating them as if he was accompanied by a full squadron of TIE Fighters;..but it was just Vader doing it all alone. His attack destroyed many small fighters and even crippled a Corellian Corvette, forcing the entire Rebel crew to abandon ship. Hera Syndulla, the greatest pilot in the Rebel Alliance, bore witness to Vaders greatness this day. When he was only 9 Vader took the prestigious title of winning the Boonta Eve Pod race on Tatooine; and was the only human to ever do so. He then used his uncanny piloting abilities to completely destroy a Separatist Command ship during the Battle of Naboo. This turned the tide of the battle into the Republics favour. After that he used Jedi starfighters to become the greatest pilot that the Jedi Order ever produced. After the rise of the Empire nothing changed. Vader was a naturally gifted pilot that used the darkside of the force to make the absolute impossible seem possible. His unpredictable, death defying, spinning manoeuvres, and his unparalleled skill in any starship he jumped in, made him by far the greatest..and deadliest pilot in the entire Star Wars Universe.

Question: What is the most realistic technology in Star Wars?
Answer: Do you remember the scene when Aunt Beru is clearly cooking fennel, in a very earthly looking food processor, at the start of A New Hope? That tin pot thing looks like the most realistic piece of kitchen equipment in any science fiction movie. In fact the whole kitchen, at the Lars homestead looks suspect; with items staight out of some Martha Stewart cooking demo. But the thing is, in Star Wars we have planet killing superweapons the size of small moons, lightsabers, hyperspace travel, and a droid manufactured for every conceivable occupation,…yet they still had to cook food like my mom in the 1980’s?! Heck,..my mom still cooks like this now! Take sci-fi works such as The Fifth Element and the Star Trek franchise. Their kitchen appliances were light years ahead of any Star Wars culinary equipment. In the Star Trek franchise replicators have been common place since time immemorial for most people, and at the simple usher of a voice command to the ships computer you can have a Tandoori chicken, or dry vodka martini in mere seconds. No mixing, no shaking, and it comes complete with a replicated cup or glass. Now that's some futuristic shit right there! In The Fifth Element Leeloo uses a similar device where once the food replicators recieve a small dehydrated pill of the chosen meal..the device instantly creates a full size chicken dinner for 5 in a whoosh of electronics! …And this movie is set on Earth in the year 2259! What the hell Star Wars!! In a galaxy set far, far away from here they still have to cook relatively similar to us on good old planet Earth; and that ‘Blue Bantha Milk’ dispenser in the corner is soo Coruscant 7-11! If this surprisingly rudimentary Star Wars technology isn't the most realistic, compared to Earthly kitchen appliances,..then I don't know what is!!

Question: Why are some alien races in Star Wars always portrayed as evil like the Hutts and Trandoshans?
Answer: What might seem evil to us humans may be culturally acceptable to some of the alien races in Star Wars, but some races in Star Wars are just born with inherent evil tendencies. The Hutts and Trandoshans view something like slavery and bloodsport as inherent qualities amongst their cultures, and have been performing such practices for untold generations. To us humans slavery, murder for hire, sex trafficking, drug smuggling, racketeering, and extortion are abhorrent behaviours unfit for our society, but for these two particular species it comes part and parcel with their ancient cultures. Both species built impressive empires based on slavery and death, much like the Zygerrians who viewed it also as a necessary part of life. Karkarodons are basically giant great white sharks, that have very angry dispositions, and a tendency to rip beings apart with their bare teeth,.. …Amanis hunt humans for sport, and make trophies of their skulls,…and Grindalids beat and force children into underground pick-pocketing syndicates. But this isn't to say that every single member of their specific species has intrinsically evil tendencies. The Zygerrians were well known for being brutal slave mongers, but on the other hand we have a record of at least one being a Jedi. Tusken Raiders are widely known to attack and murder humans who trespass against them, but as we see in The Mandalorian the humans of Mos Pelgo, and the Tuskens worked together to defeat a common foe. But without ‘evil’ looking aliens in Star Wars it would make for a very boring universe. Devaronians look like Satan himself, complete with horns and a natural immunity to fire…but in Rebels we have Cikatro Vizago who was a Devaronian crime boss turned good guy by the end of the series. Shistavanens look like the SWU version of a werewolf, and we can see one in the cantina scenes of A New Hope. But Lak Sivrak became a hero of the Rebellion, and died in the Imperial assault on Endor. Ciddarin “Cid” Scaleback was a female Trandoshan publican in The Bad Batch, and she ultimately respects and helps the good guys, and even had a soft spot for Omega. One rule to live by in the Star Wars Universe is never to judge a book by its cover.

Question: Did Emperor Palpatine collect anything?
Answer: Palpatine was an avid collector of art when he was much younger, but when he became a Sith Lord his collection mainly consisted of Sith and darkside artifacts. Proir to his ascendancy as Emperor of the entire galaxy Palpatine had an extensive collection of Sith artifacts in his luxurious Chancellors office. Of the items on bold display there were Bronzium statues of The Four Sages of Dwartii,.. a Sith Chalice,.. two enormous spirit urns,.. …and a giant stone relief on the red Sith themed walls. In one of the spirit urns he kept the ashes of his former master, Darth Plagueis. The stone relief was a huge, intricate piece depicting the Great Hyperspace Wars, and while he was Chancellor he kept this collection in full display for the Jedi, and for all to see! Whilst he was plotting his revenge against the Jedi Palpatine initially kept his collection in an old derelict building in Coruscants dank industrial sector-943, known as The Works. Here, at the Li Merge building, he kept items that couldn't be explained in front of the Jedi, such as the Great Crystal of Aantonaii, a huge Sith Holocron from Morriband, along with a large repository of other Sith Holocrons and weapons. This enormous tower was his secret lair during the Clone Wars. This collection was expanded upon at any chance that Palpatine could seize, and before he became Emperor he had his collection from The Works moved to the Grand Republic Medical facility. Palpatine took advantage of when the facility was shut down, due to CT-5555 (Fives) threatening the life of Palpatine himself; after the poor clonetrooper discovered the biochip containing Palpatines Order 66. Here he converted the lower levels into a “Sith retreat” and had the rest of his collection shipped over from The Works. After he became Emperor this all would have been moved to the new Imperial Palace; built straight on top of the old Jedi Temple. Here he kept many of the Jedi artifacts, as well as his own private Sith collection.

Question: What if Sidious didn’t steal Maul from Mother Talzin? How would the movies and shows be different?
Answer: If Darth Sidious never kidnapped Maul from Mother Talzin then he would have found another apprentice elsewhere; or he would have just taken Talzin as his acolyte..which was his initial plan from the beginning. It was only when the Sith Lord realised that the Dathomiri witch had a son that Sidious altered his plans. He sensed much more raw potential in Talzins son, and so he stole the Zabrak child and indoctrinated him into the Sith Order. This is what began the blood fued that spanned for years between the Sith and the Nightsisters. During Darth Sidious’ tutelage under his master Darth Plagueis, his intergalactic travels took him far and wide. One of his places of interest was Dathomir, for he had heard rumours of a powerful witch, and struck an unlikely accord with the Nightsister. Together they traded secrets of the force, with Sidious trying to gather all the knowledge he could from Talzin, but upon discovering young Maul the darkside apprentice himself made designs on the boys future. If he didn't take Maul he would have taken his mother, and if he didn't take her he would have searched elsewhere. Sidious knew that his master had planned to all but virtually end the rule of two by instating himself and Palpatine as eternal Sith rulers, but Palpatine also wanted the unlimited power that Plagueis had concocted for himself. It was just the inherent Sith nature of killing one's own master that drove him to think like this. This is why Sidious wanted his own apprentice, so he could become the master and Maul could step into his shoes. Palpatine would have always found a prospective alternative to Maul, and he had one with Count Dooku slowly falling to the dark. The only difference to the shows would be another unfortunate soul being bisected on Naboo and the rest, except Maul maybe chosen by Ventress during her and Talzins plan to gain vengeance on Dooku. The entire Dathomir arc would be different, or not even take place due to the non existent fued between the Sith and the Nightsisters. Just thinking about it at this point now makes my head spin…

Question: How did the Jedi defend against non-magical attacks while serving as peacekeepers for the Old Republic? Did they have a specific protocol for protection, such as using shields?
Answer: A Jedi has no need for shields of any kind, as they can use the force to substitute for a physical shield. The true test for a Jedi in combat, against non force wielders or magical practitioners, is to utilise the force to block and repel such attacks as laser bursts, grenades, missiles and other lethal projectiles. To use a shield would completely undermine their abilities as a Jedi, and a true Jedi has no use for a shield. Jedi Knights are noble and honourable fighters, and training with a shield is not part of their training regime. Most seasoned Jedi are capable of blocking projectile and laser bolt attacks, to a certain degree,..and a shield would be cumbersome and possibly limit their fighting. Even a young Jedi such as Grogu, was capable of creating a force shield to block certain attacks such as flame throwers, explosions and maybe more. Vader has even demonstrated the ability to create a powerful force shield when facing the backlash of exploding debris and flames, and even as a barrier against torrents of lava and the ocean. Aayla Secura, Anakin and Yoda create one such force barrier when faced with clouds of poisonous gas on Coruscant,.. ..and Kanan Jarrus used one of these force shields to temporarily protect members of Phoenix Squadron from an impending, enormous refinery explosion. The ability to create a force barrier is something that a Jedi strives to achieve in their training, and the deployment of shields would completely defeat the purpose of practicing and training so very hard. The Old Republic was no different to any era the Jedi fought in, and the use of shields was something considered to be beneath the Order. Only in very exceptional and rare circumstances will a Jedi use a shield.

Question: Whatever happened to the Wampa that Luke de-armed (Star Wars)?
Answer: ‘One Arm’, as she was dubbed by Skywalker, has two very interesting fates after her encounter with the young Jedi, after the Battle of Hoth. In Legends lore the female Wampa survived her ordeal, and later went on to lead a pack of other Wampas, against the intruders to their icy home. They were so good that they could break into Echo Base undetected, and attack the numerous inhabitants, who called it home since 3 ABY. In 12 ABY, Skywalker actually returns to the planet Hoth, and is recognised by the Wampa, despite nearly a decade passing since their initial encounter. The Wampa tries to exact revenge on Luke, but is ultimately slain by the Jedi. Originally when Mark Hamill filmed the scene where he chops off the Wampas arm, he believed that Luke would only scare away the creature. When the amputation was included in the final cut of the film it was stated that Hamill was horrified about it. Not that he'd care about crushing a Rancors head in the next movie, but ultimately the story would have it that the Wampa succumbs to its injury and dies;..until the 2020 Star Wars short story, Hunger, published in From a certain point of view:The Empire Strikes Back. Alleviating Hamills concerns, the story this time went that the Wampa did actually survive, and “recovered enough strength to leave its cave once again”. I guess the Wampa did knock out Luke, and kill his Tauntaun mount with one hand, so suffering the loss of just one arm wouldn't necessarily spell the creatures doom. Umm, just curious but..can I see the Wampa puppeteers arm in the bottom left of shot, when the beast is mauling the face of the poor Tauntaun?? Source; Wookiepedia, One Arm (Canon & Legends)

Question: What would happen if a small child bumped into Darth Vader or Darth Sidious?
Answer: Darth Vader and Darth Sidious have both bumped into small children, when they have been on their dark side rampages. During the great Jedi purge, directly after the Clone Wars, Darth Vader was with his legion of stormtroopers on the now Imperial held Wookiee home world of Kashyyyk. Amidst the chaotic battle, Vader encounters a straggler. Jedi knight, Kento Marek. Slaying Kento in a lightsaber duel, Vader and his men proceed to continue their purge when Vader discovered a small boy. The boy was Kento Marek’s son. Galen Marek. This now orphaned child displayed such raw and unprecedented talent in the force, that he easily force snatched Vader’s crimson lightsaber straight from his hand. Vader was so impressed with this small boy’s connection to the force, that he abducted him and took him as his secret apprentice. Trained for years in the dark side at the hands of one of the cruelest masters, young Galen was dubbed Starkiller. He went on to defy his former dark master and paid for it with his life. Darth Sidious, whilst apprenticing to Darth Plagueis, was on Dathomir when a Nightsister approached him with her infant child. In a bid to grant her son a better life with a supreme being, she turned him over to Sidious. She sensed his dark authority as soon as she gazed at him across a marketplace. Sidious, knowing about these Dathomirian witches’ uncanny dark side abilities, had Maul trained in the dark side on Mustafar, far away from the eyes of the Jedi. Trained as a fledgling Sith assassin, Maul went on in time to become one of the most deadly dark side opponents that any Jedi would hesitate to engage in combat. In summary, when two of the greatest Sith lords to ever live encounter small children, they sometimes end up becoming galactic monsters feared by all who hear their names.
